title: Fun stories from building OpenRouter and where all this is going - Alex Atallah, OpenRouter
talk_summary: Alex Atallah recounts OpenRouter's evolution from a model-discovery site into a multi-provider inference marketplace, arguing inference is a commodity and the future is multi-model. The one concrete engineering story is an AI-native middleware/plugin layer that augments any model with web search and PDF parsing, transforming streamed outputs in-flight.

takeaways.what_they_do: Aggregate many providers per model and route/fallback across them to boost uptime and pick better prices, normalizing tool calls and caching so the caller doesn't care which provider serves.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we help developers basically get uptime boosting and you can see like the delta ... how much we can boost uptime just by aggregating lots of different providers for a model

takeaways.technique: AI-native middleware plugins that transform streamed output
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of only pre-flight MCP tool calls, they run middleware around inference that can call MCPs and also augment/annotate results on the way back to the user, live in the stream.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it can also augment the results on the way back to the user ... every language model can just kind of tap in to this plugin and get web annotations as results are being fed back to users in real time

takeaways.what_they_do: They standardized wildly different provider stream-cancellation policies because dropping a stream can still bill you for the whole completion or extra tokens.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Sometimes if you just drop a stream the the the the inference provider will bill you for the entire thing. Sometimes it won't.

takeaways.technique: Route by capability/price data, not model hopping
takeaways.what_they_do: They publish per-model latency/throughput/price data and note usage is sticky per task rather than users constantly switching models; routing is framed as the key cost lever.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we think inference will be like a dominant operating expense and selecting and routing will be crucial
